author: product-requirements-expert
title: Read-only specialty directory page
summary: A read-only page lists every specialty by its stored name, each with the veterinarians who hold it shown by full name, all specialties on one page with no paging.
acceptance_criteria: Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then every specialty is listed by its stored name, each with the veterinarians who hold it shown by full name in first-name-then-last-name order
Given a veterinarian who holds no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears under no specialty
Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then all of them appear on a single page with no paging
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged)
notes: Read-only view over the existing cached veterinarian/specialty collection. NG-2 unchanged; no existing requirement altered. Prose keeps to behavior per the PRD boundary rule — the page's route and rendering mechanism are for system-design.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Reuses the existing vet feature package and the server-rendered read-only pattern already carried by VetController (system-design.md#contracts, ADR 2026-07-31-server-side-rendering-with-thymeleaf). The one adjustment: a second GET handler on VetController that inverts the vet->specialties graph exposed by Vet.getSpecialties() into a specialty->veterinarians projection, rendered by a new Thymeleaf template paralleling vets/vetList. No new repository, no new cache, no service layer, no new domain type. system-design.md Contracts row for VetController updated to carry REQ-VET-003.
integration_points: New handler @GetMapping("/specialties.html") on VetController returning view name vets/specialtyList; route name parallels the existing /vets.html convention.

Data source is vetRepository.findAll() (no-arg, @Cacheable("vets")) — the same cached collection the vet list uses; specialties arrive eagerly via Vet's EAGER ManyToMany. No new repository call and no new cache region.

Controller builds a specialty-keyed projection for the model: for every specialty held across all vets, collect the vets holding it. Order specialties by stored name; order veterinarians within each by a stable key (last-then-first reads naturally for a directory; stable order is the bar per Veterinarian-directory edge case 1). A SortedMap<Specialty,List<Vet>> or Map<String,List<Vet>> keyed by name keeps the projection in the controller, consistent with how showVetList assembles its pagination model.
Template renders each veterinarian's full name as firstName + ' ' + lastName — the exact expression vetList.html already uses (produces "Helen Leary").

i18n: reuse existing message keys only — 'specialties' and 'name'/'vets' already exist in all 11 bundles. Any NEW user-facing key must be added to every messages*.properties or the REQ-LANG-002 build-time key-parity test fails; the prd-entry file_targets omit the bundles, so a new key would require expanding the target set.

patterns.description: existing read-only GET handler + model-assembly-in-controller pattern to mirror for /specialties.html
full-name rendering (firstName + ' ' + lastName) and #{none}/#{specialties} key usage to reuse

risks.risk: "Every specialty the clinic knows" vs. specialties reachable through vets: deriving the projection from vetRepository.findAll() surfaces only specialties held by at least one vet. A specialty held by zero vets would not appear.
risks.mitigation: Acceptable and non-observable under current design: all three seeded specialties (radiology, surgery, dentistry) are held, and NG-2 forbids managing specialties through the app, so the specialty set is fixed seed data with no unheld member. The prd-entry deliberately scopes this to the cached vet/specialty collection (no SpecialtyRepository in file_targets). If an unheld specialty must ever list, introduce a SpecialtyRepository then — out of scope now.

risks.risk: Veterinarians holding no specialty must be excluded (acceptance criterion 2). Inverting the graph over held specialties drops zero-specialty vets automatically — but a naive implementation that seeds the map from the full vet roster would wrongly include them.
risks.mitigation: Build the projection by iterating each vet's specialties (skip vets with an empty specialty set); never seed keys from the roster. The test theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOmitVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty pins this.

risks.risk: Introducing a new heading/label key would break REQ-LANG-002 key-parity across 11 bundles if added to only one.
risks.mitigation: Prefer the existing 'specialties'/'name' keys for headings; if a new key is unavoidable, add it to all messages*.properties in the same slice and note the expanded file_targets.

notes: Verdict minor, not covered, because a small load-bearing addition exists (the specialty->vet inversion and a new template) and system-design.md#contracts was edited to map REQ-VET-003 onto VetController. No ADR: route naming and controller-assembled projection both follow committed conventions with no hard-to-reverse trade-off. Basis for the covering-code claims is grep + direct file reads of the vet package (VetController, Vet, VetRepository, vetList.html, messages.properties); IDE oracle not consulted. Navigation: REQ-SYS-001 names only owner search and the veterinarian directory, and the prd-entry omits the layout template — the specialty page is reachable by direct URL and adding it to nav is out of this slice's scope. No design-doc-autofix records present; autofix audit skipped.
